title: Lo, What a Glorious Sight Appears
description: Lo, What a Glorious Sight Appears in Tonic Solfa to ST. PETER, doh is Eb: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 6 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words for his Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707), Book I, collected from the Scriptures, hymn 21, headed “A vision of the kingdom of Christ among men, Rev. 21. 1-4”.
Watts' hymns were printed without tunes and sung to any tune of their metre, Common Metre (8.6.8.6). This page sets the words to ST. PETER; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Lo, what a glo-rious sight ap-pears To our be-liev-ing eyes! The earth and sea are pass'd a-way, And the old roll-ing skies.

lines: Lo, what a glorious sight appears
The earth and sea are pass'd away,
From the third heaven where God resides,
"The God of glory down to men
"Men the dear objects of his grace,
"His own soft hand shall wipe the tears
"And pains, and groans, and griefs, and fears,
How long, dear Saviour, O how long,
Fly swifter round, ye wheels of time,

source: Isaac Watts, Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707)
licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain; set to ST. PETER by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
